question.text: The displacement and the increase in the velocity of a moving particle in the time interval of <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi>t</mi></math> to <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn><mo>)</mo><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> are <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>125</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math> and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>50</mn><mo> </mo><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi><mo> </mo><msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi><mrow><mo>-</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msup></math>, respectively. The distance travelled by the particle in <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mo>(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>2</mn><msup><mo>)</mo><mtext>th </mtext></msup><mi mathvariant="normal">s</mi></math> is ___________ <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mi mathvariant="normal">m</mi></math>.

solution.text:
Considering acceleration is constant, we can write

v=u+at

As increase in velocity in 1 s is given as 50 m s-1, therefore

⇒a=50 m s-2

Now, displacement covered between given time interval is, 

125=ut+12at2

⇒125=u+a2

⇒u=100 m s-1

Velocity after 1 s will be, v=100+50=150 m s-1

Therefore, displacement covered in t+1 s to t+2 s will 

∴Snth=vt'+12at'2, where t'=1 s

=175 m
